Thank you for your feedback, and the invitation. While I personally like SourceFed and find it a pleasant alternative to watching mainstream media news, this (these) post(s) were my way of asking the community what it thinks of SourceFed. While it (they) haven't gotten much love, I haven't seen a backlash against them either. While I cannot promise you I won't ever post from SourceFed again (sometimes they have truly brilliant segments), I do promise not to make a habit of it, and to respect moderator wishes if they start getting pulled, or (and my two cents is that THIS is how it should be) community wishes if they start getting large amounts of downvotes or negative comments.

Clarification on "my two cents" : Voting sites exist under the pretense that communities will upvote what they like and downvote what they do not. Since this voting will push a thread up or down by themselves, it is my personal opinion that rules on the subject are unnecessary as the community will "enforce it's will" without the mods needing to step in and play arbiters. I would also just like to point out that this is why I left Reddit. Despite threads receiving overwhelmingly positive voting, mods would step in and remove them because they "broke the rules." In my opinion, if the community wants to see content, mods should step back and allow them as a community to make that decision.

But that's just my two cents and, as I just pointed out, the community (not individuals within it) should be able to decide.
